standard_prerequisites.name: Maximal chains of primes above a given prime

core_obligations: Use the dimension formula for the closed set of a prime to replace the transcendence degree by the dimension of the vanishing set (proof lines 28452-28454).

Choose a maximal chain of primes above the given prime and compare it with chains inside the local ring, deducing the displayed formula for the local dimension and finishing with a maximum over finitely many chains (proof lines 28455-28479).
proof_roadmap: Replace the transcendence degree by the dimension of a closed set (proof lines 28451-28454).
Compare chains above the prime with chains in the local ring (proof lines 28455-28480).
difficulty_reason: For a finite type algebra S over a field and a prime p, the lemma computes the local dimension at the corresponding point as the dimension of the local ring plus the transcendence degree of the residue field (statement lines 28438-28449). The proof does not quote the dimension formula in the abstract: it identifies the transcendence degree with the dimension of the vanishing set of p, then examines a maximal chain of primes above p and compares chains in the spectrum with chains inside the local ring, writing the local dimension as a maximum over the finitely many chains obtained (proof lines 28451-28480). The comparison of the two kinds of chains is the step that produces the formula. H2.
